hero.lead: A nation of 255.2 million on the Indus, which has drawn $4.8 billion from the IMF since 2024 and rebuilt its reserves to about $21.5 billion.

capital.heading: Pakistan has rebuilt its reserves review by review. Next, every child reading by ten.

record.text: Total public debt at end-June 2026, around 68.3% of GDP; external debt $98.1 billion
Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility: disbursed to date; about $1.2 billion more on Board approval of the reviews agreed in October 2026
International bond in two dollar tranches, 5½ and 10 years, coupons 7.50% and 7.90%, marked in London on 29 September 2026
New Saudi deposit received in fiscal year 2026; $5 billion of earlier deposits rolled over for three years
Public Resources for Inclusive Development, approved 19 December 2025: funds released against results in tax, spending systems and subsidies

register.name: International bond, two dollar tranches
register.detail: $1.75 billion, 5½ years, coupon 7.50% · $1.25 billion, 10 years, coupon 7.90% · Marked at the London Stock Exchange 29 September 2026
register.note: Investor demand of nearly $6 billion
register.text: A $3 billion sovereign Eurobond in two dollar tranches, which drew nearly $6 billion of investor demand, almost twice the amount issued. The London Stock Exchange marked the issuance on 29 September 2026.

register.name: Panda bond, Pakistan’s first
register.detail: Issued 15 May 2026 · 3 years, coupon 2.5% · Partial debt guarantee from AIIB, with ADB support
register.note: About $250 million (Ministry of Finance); about $258 million (AIIB)
register.text: Pakistan’s first sovereign panda bond, in renminbi, enabled by a partial debt guarantee from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, with the Asian Development Bank also supporting it. Its proceeds are to support sustainable and climate-resilient infrastructure in water, energy and health.

register.name: Eurobond, private placement
register.detail: Issued 24 April 2026 · 3 years, coupon 6.975%, maturing 24 April 2029
register.note: Private placement
register.text: A three-year dollar bond placed privately with investors in April 2026. Eurobond repayments in fiscal year 2026 came to $1.8 billion.

register.name: Sindh Property Revenues Enhancement Program (Sindh PREP)
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2026 · Includes a $40 million investment component · 25 Karachi local councils and 20 other urban councils
register.note: Karachi property tax from about $8.5 million to a target of $85 million a year
register.text: Raises property tax collection in Karachi’s 25 local councils, home to 3.58 million people, and puts about 70% of it back into drainage, sewerage, schools, fire stations, roads and street lighting. Property surveys extend to 20 local councils in Sindh’s other cities. It pays for the water, shelter and education services that cities provide.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Third review completed 8 May 2026 · Fourth EFF and third RSF reviews agreed by staff 7 October 2026, subject to Executive Board approval
register.note: Disbursed to date; about $1.3 billion released in May 2026
register.text: A 37-month Extended Fund Facility approved 25 September 2024 and a 28-month Resilience and Sustainability Facility approved 9 May 2025. On Board approval of the reviews agreed in October 2026, about $1.0 billion under the EFF and about $210 million under the RSF become available, bringing disbursements to about $5.7 billion. Gross reserves rose to about $21.5 billion by end-September 2026.

register.name: Grid Stability Enhancement Project
register.detail: Approved 9 July 2026 · First phase of the 10-year BEST-PAK programme
register.note: Compensators, reactors and capacitor banks at 29 substations
register.text: Installs compensators at three 500 kV substations and reactors and capacitor banks at 26 grid substations, bringing 640 MW of curtailed wind power onto the grid and avoiding about 832,500 tons of CO₂ a year. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Public Resources for Inclusive Development, first operations
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · Federal $600 million · Sindh $100 million · Multiphase programme of up to $1.35 billion · Disbursed against results
register.note: Tax, public financial management, subsidies and statistics
register.text: Funds are released only when results are met: tax reform, a stronger financial management system with e-procurement, targeted subsidies and better national statistics. In Sindh it supports more equitable financing for primary health facilities and more funding for schools. It widens the fiscal room that pays for health and education.

register.name: Punjab Inclusive Cities Program
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2025 · 16 secondary cities
register.note: Water, sanitation and drainage for about 4.5 million people
register.text: Upgrades water supply, sewerage, wastewater treatment and stormwater drainage in 16 secondary cities of Punjab, and solid waste management for 2 million more people. It aims to lower child stunting and waterborne disease, and serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Education and water in Balochistan
register.detail: Approved 24 June 2025 · GRADES-Balochistan $100 million · Balochistan Water Security and Productivity Improvement $94 million
register.note: Schools and water
register.text: GRADES-Balochistan will benefit 250,000 students and support 5,000 teachers; the water project brings better basic water supply to 500,000 people in the Kachi Plain and Quetta. Together they serve the education and water standards in Pakistan’s largest province.

register.name: Resilient and Accessible Microfinance (RAM) Project
register.detail: Approved 18 March 2025 · Co-financed by a $23 million Global Shield grant
register.note: Nearly 1.89 million people, more than 1 million of them women
register.text: Expands microcredit, including recovery loans, and sets up a Climate Risk Fund to protect microfinance borrowers against climate shocks. It reaches nearly 1.89 million people, more than 1 million of them women and over 350,000 young people, and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Insurance Transformation Program, subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 18 June 2026 · Policy-based loan
register.note: Insurance for farmers, women and vulnerable households
register.text: Supports insurance reforms and products for farmers, women and vulnerable households, including parametric insurance, and develops private pensions to mobilise long-term savings. It protects livelihoods against shocks.

register.name: State enterprise reform and Sindh coastal resilience
register.detail: Approved 12 December 2025 · Accelerating SOE Transformation Program, results-based loan $400 million · Sindh Coastal Resilience Sector Project $140 million, with a $20 million grant and a $20 million loan from the Green Climate Fund
register.note: 150,000 hectares of farmland safeguarded in Badin, Sujawal and Thatta
register.text: The $400 million results-based loan supports reform of state-owned enterprises. The $140 million coastal project safeguards 150,000 hectares of farmland, restores 22,000 hectares of forest and improves the lives of more than 500,000 people, protecting food and livelihoods on the Sindh coast.

register.name: Punjab farm mechanization, STEM schooling and nursing
register.detail: Approved 6 December 2025 · Mechanization $124 million · STEM secondary education $107 million, results-based · Nursing and health workforce $150 million
register.note: 220,000 farm households; nursing centres in Lahore, Multan and Rawalpindi
register.text: Three projects in Punjab: climate-resilient, low-carbon farm mechanization for 220,000 rural households; a results-based programme for science, technology, engineering and mathematics in secondary schools; and nursing reform with three centres of excellence. They serve the food, education and health standards.

register.name: Second Power Transmission Strengthening Project
register.detail: Approved 20 November 2025 · Ordinary capital $285 million · Concessional $45 million · National Grid Company of Pakistan
register.note: About 290 km of new transmission line
register.text: Builds a transmission line of about 290 km to carry up to 3,200 MW of clean power from hydropower plants. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Lahore Wastewater and Drainage Management Project
register.detail: Approved 9 October 2025 · Sovereign financing · Treatment plant at Babu Sabu funded by AFD
register.note: Wastewater and drainage services in Lahore
register.text: Improves wastewater and drainage services in Lahore and eases urban flooding, alongside a wastewater treatment plant at Babu Sabu financed by the Agence Française de Développement. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Flood Protection and Dike Improvement on the Indus River in Sindh
register.detail: Signed 7 September 2026 · Grant · Larkana District
register.note: JPY 2,585 million
register.text: A Japanese grant to reduce the risk of dike breaches on the lower Indus in Larkana District, Sindh. It protects homes, farms and livelihoods from floods.

register.name: Saudi Arabia, deposits
register.detail: New deposit of $3 billion received in fiscal year 2026 · Earlier deposit of $5 billion rolled over for three years
register.note: New deposit; $5 billion of earlier deposits rolled over
register.text: Saudi Arabia placed a new $3 billion deposit in fiscal year 2026 and rolled over its earlier $5 billion deposit for three years. The deposits support Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves.

register.name: China, bilateral deposits
register.detail: Rolled over for one year in fiscal year 2026
register.note: Rolled over for one year
register.text: China rolled over $4.0 billion of bilateral deposits for one year in fiscal year 2026. With the Saudi deposits, they support Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves.

register.name: Bank Alfalah, diversified payment rights note
register.detail: Approved by the IFC Board 27 May 2026 · Announced 20 August 2026 · Pakistan’s first diversified payment rights note
register.note: Up to $100 million from IFC
register.text: IFC’s investment in Pakistan’s first diversified payment rights note, a new source of long-term international funding for Pakistan’s banks. Longer funding lets banks lend to businesses and households.

register.name: Reko Diq copper-gold mine, first phase
register.detail: Approved 22 August 2025 · Senior loans of up to $300 million · Partial credit guarantee of $110 million for the Government of Balochistan’s equity · Loan documents to be finalised
register.note: Copper concentrate expected from late 2028
register.text: Asian Development Bank financing for the Reko Diq mine in Chagai, Balochistan, built and operated by Barrick, which owns 50%. The guarantee covers the equity of the Government of Balochistan, so the province can share in the earnings of its own minerals.

register.name: Acumen Climate Action Pakistan Fund (FP229)
register.detail: Approved 6 March 2024 · $25 million equity and $3 million grant · Total value $90 million · Agreement executed 14 November 2024
register.note: 13.1 million people with increased resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund investment in an $80 million fund for climate adaptation in Pakistan, with a $10 million technical assistance envelope. It serves the food and livelihood standards for farmers facing climate risk.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 40 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy bazaar street in Lahore

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Wheat fields on the irrigated plains of Punjab, Pakistan

items.name: The Cities
items.label: Live in towns and cities
items.text: Dense cities make every pipe, cable and clinic serve more people for each dollar spent.
items.alt: The modern skyline of Karachi, Pakistan, at dusk

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The Indus River flowing through the mountains of northern Pakistan

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Wind turbines of the Jhimpir wind corridor in Sindh, Pakistan

items.name: Engro Fertilizers
items.text: A Pakistani fertiliser maker. In December 2025 IFC announced a partial credit guarantee of up to PKR 33.6 billion (about $120 million) on a Standard Chartered Pakistan loan for plant maintenance and farmer programmes, IFC’s first local currency investment in Pakistan.

items.name: Pakistan Mortgage Refinance Company
items.text: A mortgage refinance company that helps lenders offer affordable home loans, with a focus on underserved regions. IFC agreed in 2020 to invest up to PKR 500 million (about $3.2 million) of equity, when Pakistan’s housing deficit stood at 10 million units.

items.name: Shams Power
items.text: A developer of small rooftop and ground-mounted solar plants at commercial and industrial sites across Pakistan, with 27 projects and 25 MW installed by January 2024. GuarantCo, part of PIDG, guaranteed 75% of a PKR 1.5 billion Bank Alfalah loan to add about 10 MW more.

items.name: The Citizens Foundation
items.text: A non-profit network of schools across Pakistan, with 320,000 students enrolled in 2,261 school units. Its 16,500 faculty members are all women (2025 annual report of TCF Canada).

items.name: Indus Hospital & Health Network
items.text: A countrywide network of 12 secondary and tertiary care hospitals and more than 100 primary care facilities, with Pakistan’s largest paediatric oncology unit. Its services are free of cost to patients (data as of January 2025).

items.name: ASA Microfinance Bank (Pakistan)
items.text: A microfinance bank serving more than 800,000 clients through more than 400 branches and service centres. In August 2026 IFC lent it $10 million for four years to expand finance for women borrowers.
